proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 \mathcal C_{\to}(G)
 :=\{H\in\mathfrak D(V):H\equiv_EG,\ E^{\leftrightarrow}(H)=\varnothing\}.
\]
The premise \(E^{\leftrightarrow}(G)=\varnothing\) implies \(G\in\mathcal C_{\to}(G)\), so this family is nonempty.  By the published directed greatest-element theorem, \(\mathrm{lem{:}directed\text{-}greatest\text{-}published}\), there is \(\widehat G_{\to}\in\mathcal C_{\to}(G)\) such that \(H\subseteq\widehat G_{\to}\) for every \(H\in\mathcal C_{\to}(G)\).

Let \(H_1,H_2\in\mathcal C_{\to}(G)\), and let \(K=H_1\cup H_2\), where the union is taken over directed edges and the bidirected edge set remains empty.  Then
\[
 H_1\subseteq K\subseteq\widehat G_{\to}.
\]
Both endpoint graphs are E-equivalent.  The interval conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem{:}antitonicity}\) therefore gives
\[
 \mathcal I_E(K)=\mathcal I_E(H_1)=\mathcal I_E(G).
\]
Thus \(K\in\mathcal C_{\to}(G)\), proving binary directed-edge-union closure.

Because \(U_{\to}=V\times V\) is finite, \(\mathcal C_{\to}(G)\) is finite.  Define
\[
 \overline G_{\to}
 =\left(V,
   \bigcup_{H\in\mathcal C_{\to}(G)}E^{\to}(H),
   \varnothing\right).
\]
Since every member of \(\mathcal C_{\to}(G)\) is contained in \(\widehat G_{\to}\), one has \(\overline G_{\to}\subseteq\widehat G_{\to}\).  Conversely, \(\widehat G_{\to}\) itself occurs in the union, so \(\widehat G_{\to}\subseteq\overline G_{\to}\).  Hence
\[
 \overline G_{\to}=\widehat G_{\to}\in\mathcal C_{\to}(G).
\]
It contains every member of the family and is therefore greatest; antisymmetry of edge inclusion makes it the unique greatest member.

The family \(\mathcal C_{\to}(G)\) is a subfamily of \(\{H\in\mathfrak D(V):H\equiv_EG\}\).  Taking componentwise unions in \(\mathrm{def{:}greatest}\) consequently gives
\[
 E^{\to}(\overline G_{\to})\subseteq E^{\to}(G^\star),
 \qquad
 E^{\leftrightarrow}(\overline G_{\to})=\varnothing
 \subseteq E^{\leftrightarrow}(G^\star),
\]
so \(\overline G_{\to}\subseteq G^\star\).  This inclusion can be strict.  Indeed, take \(V=\{v\}\).  Let \(G_{\to}\) have the single directed loop \(v\to v\), and let \(G_{\leftrightarrow}\) have the single bidirected loop \(v\leftrightarrow v\).  If either \(A\) or \(B\) is empty, both E-separation statements hold vacuously.  Otherwise \(A=B=\{v\}\).  For \(C=\varnothing\), \(\operatorname{Lift}(G_{\to})\) contains the one-edge open walk \(v_0\to v_1\), while \(\operatorname{Lift}(G_{\leftrightarrow})\) contains the one-edge open walk \(v_0\leftrightarrow v_1\); hence the singleton query is a dependence in both graphs.  For \(C=\{v\}\),
\[
 D(B,C)=\{v_0\},
\]
so the source endpoint is conditioned and the query is separated in both graphs.  These cases exhaust \(\mathcal P(V)^3\), proving \(G_{\to}\equiv_EG_{\leftrightarrow}\).  The empty directed graph is not equivalent to \(G_{\to}\), because it separates \(v_0\) from \(v_1\) given the empty set.  Thus the directed greatest member for \(G_{\to}\) is \(G_{\to}\), whereas \(G^\star\) also contains the bidirected loop supplied by \(G_{\leftrightarrow}\).  Therefore \(G_{\to}\subsetneq G^\star\), as claimed.

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite directed graph \(G=(V,E^{\to}(G))\), there exists a directed graph \(\widehat G\) on \(V\) such that \(\widehat G\equiv_E G\) and \(H\subseteq\widehat G\) for every directed graph \(H\) on \(V\) satisfying \(H\equiv_EG\).

source.verbatim_statement: The Markov equivalence class of \(G\) contains a greatest element with respect to the partial order \(\subseteq\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Theorem 3.12 of the cited PMLR paper.

proposed.statement:
If \(E^{\leftrightarrow}(G)=\varnothing\), then the directed subfamily
\[
\{H\in\mathfrak D(V):H\equiv_E G,\ E^{\leftrightarrow}(H)=\varnothing\}
\]
is closed under directed-edge union and has the unique greatest member
\[
\left(V,
\bigcup_{\substack{H\equiv_EG\\E^{\leftrightarrow}(H)=\varnothing}}E^{\to}(H),
\varnothing\right).
\]
This is the valid directed-subclass reduction.  It is a subgraph of the unrestricted \(G^\star\), but equality with \(G^\star\) can fail.
proposed.justification: This is the required standard-case sanity check.
proposed.gap: It is a reduction, not a novelty claim.
proposed.consumer: Fully observed E-discovery is recovered unchanged.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The directed reduction is proved from the published directed greatest-element theorem and antitonicity, independently of the still-open unrestricted mixed greatest-representative target; its dependency list must record that actual proof spine.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove that every profile-changing edge occurring in an E-equivalent comparison graph is individually safe to add to the base graph.
open_obligations.obstruction: The fixed-profile splice only replaces edges already represented by directed paths or by an occupied cross-SCC bidirected rectangle in the base lift.  Equality of E-models supplies only past-to-future separation queries with the target-dependent conditioning set \(D(B,C)\); it has not been shown to determine the endpoint marks, copy indices, ancestry certificates, and SCC-tail certificates needed to splice an arbitrary profile-changing edge.  The published greatest-element theorem for homogeneous weak \(\mu\)-equivalence cannot be imported: E-equivalence restricts both endpoint layers and conditioning sets in a target-dependent, non-homogeneous way, and E-separation is not \(\mu\)-separation on the original DMG.
open_obligations.attempted: The fixed-profile replacement, antitonicity, first-new-edge minimality, singleton composition, a potential-parent/potential-sibling reduction patterned on \(\mu\)-separation, and a two-copy-lift reduction to homogeneous weak equivalence were checked.  The latter two routes require marked connectivity information not encoded by any declared frozen node.  Independently, the prescribed exhaustive gate tested every one of the \(384168\) loop-free five-vertex bases with at most five edges.  It performed \(12105891\) signature comparisons, covering \(708990\) individually safe additions and \(129303\) same-signature collisions, and found no failure.  Exhaustive loop-inclusive checks through three vertices also found no failure, but neither finite calculation proves the universal claim.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For every \(e\in E(\Gamma(G))\setminus E(G)\), the fixed-profile theorem gives \(G\equiv_E\Gamma(G)\), while
\[
 G\subseteq G+e\subseteq\Gamma(G).
\]
The interval part of antitonicity therefore proves \(G+e\equiv_EG\).  This covers exactly the directed completions internal to a non-singleton SCC, the completions of an already occupied incoming-to-SCC support, and the bidirected completions of an already occupied cross-SCC rectangle, with both loop conventions retained by \(\Gamma\).  It does not prove safety for an edge that changes this profile.  The independent finite falsification gate over the loop-free five-vertex universe checked all \(384168\) bases having at most five edges, all \(400\) nontrivial singleton queries per signature, \(708990\) individually safe additions, and \(129303\) same-signature collisions; no unsafe admissible union or collision union was found.  This finite computation is evidence only and supplies no universal implication.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Establish unrestricted binary-union closure for two E-equivalent finite directed mixed graphs.
open_obligations.obstruction: The finite order argument is complete, but it requires unrestricted single-edge transfer.  Antitonicity only controls intervals between comparable equivalent graphs and gives no conclusion for the union of two incomparable representatives.
open_obligations.attempted: The edges of one representative were enumerated for successive transfer, and the full finite equivalence class was then enumerated for a final union.  This closes every order-theoretic step but leaves the first profile-changing edge addition exactly at the unresolved transfer obligation.  The five-vertex sparse gate found no counterexample but supplies no finite reduction theorem.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Assuming the still-open unrestricted single-edge transfer theorem, binary-union closure follows without any further graph-theoretic premise.  Given \(G\equiv_EH\), enumerate the finite difference as
\[
 E(H)\setminus E(G)=\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\},
 \qquad K_0=G,\qquad K_r=G+\{e_1,\ldots,e_r\}.
\]
Inductively, \(K_{r-1}\equiv_EH\) and \(e_r\in E(H)\setminus E(K_{r-1})\), so transfer gives \(K_r\equiv_EK_{r-1}\).  Hence \(K_m=G\cup H\equiv_EG\).  Since the full edge universe is finite, the E-equivalence class is finite; iterating binary union over all its members proves that the graph defined in \(\mathrm{def{:}greatest}\) belongs to the class and contains every member.  Antisymmetry gives uniqueness.  Thus the order-theoretic reduction is complete, and its sole missing premise is unrestricted transfer.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove that the union of all individually admissible profile-changing edges is E-equivalent to the base graph.
open_obligations.obstruction: Individual signature preservation does not imply joint preservation for a general antitone independence map.  For this E-model the missing joint step is equivalent to the still-open unrestricted greatest-representative closure.
open_obligations.attempted: Singleton composition was used to turn each admissible one-edge extension into an E-equivalent graph, and the interval property was used in the reverse direction conditional on an in-class greatest representative.  This proves the exact identity conditionally but does not prove that the unrestricted union remains in the class.  The exhaustive sparse gate directly tested all-admissible unions in its finite region and found no failure.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditionally on unrestricted greatest-representative closure, the target reduces exactly to observable singleton signatures.  First, if \(e\in\operatorname{Adm}(G)\), then \(\Sigma_E(G+e)=\Sigma_E(G)\) by definition, and singleton composition gives \(G+e\equiv_EG\).  Hence \(e\in E(G^\star)\setminus E(G)\).  Conversely, if \(e\in E(G^\star)\setminus E(G)\), then
\[
 G\subseteq G+e\subseteq G^\star,
 \qquad G\equiv_EG^\star,
\]
and antitonicity gives \(G+e\equiv_EG\), hence \(e\in\operatorname{Adm}(G)\).  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Adm}(G)=E(G^\star)\setminus E(G),
 \qquad G+\operatorname{Adm}(G)=G^\star,
 \qquad \mathcal I_E(G+\operatorname{Adm}(G))=\mathcal I_E(G).
\]
No positivity, rank, support, boundary, or limiting condition occurs: the argument is finite and purely graphical.  The unresolved premise is precisely that \(G^\star\equiv_EG\) for the unrestricted finite-DMG class.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Show that the componentwise union enumerated from the singleton oracle is itself E-equivalent to the unknown graph over the unrestricted finite-DMG class.
open_obligations.obstruction: The finite query reduction and enumeration compute the union exactly, but identifying that observable union with an in-class greatest representative is precisely unrestricted union closure.
open_obligations.attempted: The singleton table was reduced to \(Q=n^2 2^{n-1}\) nontrivial queries, exhaustive graph enumeration was specified, and the compelled-edge deletion equivalence was proved conditional on greatestness.  No independent route makes the enumerated unrestricted union E-equivalent without resolving transfer or union closure.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The queried table has
\[
 n^2\,\bigl|\{C:C\subseteq V\setminus\{a\}\}\bigr|
 =n^2 2^{n-1}=Q
\]
entries.  Every omitted singleton query has \(a\in C\), so its source \(a_0\) belongs to \(D(\{b\},C)\) and the query is separated.  Thus the queried table determines the full singleton signature, and singleton composition determines \(\mathcal I_E\).  Since \(\mathfrak D(V)\) is finite, exhaustive comparison with this table computes both the componentwise union and the edge intersection of all matching graphs.  Conditional on unrestricted union closure, the computed union is the in-class graph \(G^\star\).

For the compelled-edge test, fix \(e\in E(G^\star)\).  If \(\Sigma_E(G^\star-e)=\Sigma_E(G^\star)\), composition makes \(G^\star-e\) E-equivalent to \(G^\star\), so an equivalent graph omits \(e\) and \(e\notin\operatorname{Comp}(G)\).  Conversely, if \(e\notin\operatorname{Comp}(G)\), some \(K\equiv_EG\) omits \(e\).  Greatestness yields
\[
 K\subseteq G^\star-e\subseteq G^\star,
\]
and the interval property yields \(G^\star-e\equiv_EG^\star\), hence equal signatures.  Taking contrapositives proves
\[
 e\in\operatorname{Comp}(G)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Sigma_E(G^\star-e)\ne\Sigma_E(G^\star).
\]
The enumeration, query count, and deletion criterion are therefore complete; only the unrestricted in-class union assertion remains open.
